basics.label: Professor of Herbology, Cryptobotanical Researcher & Field Operative
basics.name: Neville Longbottom
basics.summary: Highly accomplished Herbology scholar and internationally recognised experimental botanist with extensive experience in field research, species documentation, and conservation of magically-active flora. Decorated veteran with a proven record of leadership and resilience in hazardous environments. Developed and led botanical surveys, resulting in the discovery and formal documentation of previously uncatalogued magical species. Adept at independent fieldwork, managing complex biological systems, and operating under pressure. Former Auror with tactical field experience. Strong background in the scientific classification of challenging magical specimens.

projects.description: A multi-institution conservation programme aimed at cataloguing, seed-banking, and cultivating endangered magical plant species. Partners include the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew, the Beauxbatons Botanical Institute, and two Scandinavian magical natural history museums.
highlights: Catalogued 63 species of endangered magical flora across the Hogwarts grounds and surrounding region
Established a living seed bank of over 200 species in the Hogwarts greenhouse complex
Developed propagation protocols for four species previously considered uncultivable in captivity
Trained twelve botanical researchers from partner institutions in magical plant handling and cultivation

publications.name: Aggressive Cultivar Suppression in Hogwarts Grounds: A 20-Year Survey
publications.publisher: Journal of the Wizarding Botanical Society
publications.summary: Longitudinal study examining the spread and management of invasive magical plant species in the Hogwarts grounds and Forbidden Forest, offering a long-term dataset on inter-species dynamics in a managed magical environment.

publications.name: Mandrake Restorative Draught Potency: The Impact of Soil Composition and Maturation Rate
publications.summary: Research paper demonstrating that modifications to Mandrake cultivation soil composition and controlled maturation timing significantly improve the potency and reliability of the standard Restorative Draught formula. Adopted into revised St Mungo's treatment protocols.

publications.name: Teaching Herbology to Traumatised Learners: A Framework for Post-Conflict Magical Education
publications.summary: Practitioner-focused paper drawing on Neville's experience teaching post-war students at Hogwarts, proposing a trauma-sensitive pedagogical framework applicable across magical subjects with particular relevance to Herbology's sensory and practical elements.

references.name: Harry Potter, Head Auror — Ministry of Magic
references.reference: Neville is one of the bravest people I've ever known — and I mean that in a specific, evidence-based way. He spent an entire year leading resistance against Death Eaters while the rest of us were on the run, took punishment that would have broken most adults, and then showed up for the Battle without hesitation. He destroyed the last Horcrux while I was supposed to be dead. That sort of person, you don't forget. As a professor he's exceptional — every student who's come through his Herbology class comes out of it actually caring about the subject.

references.name: Professor Minerva McGonagall, Headmistress — Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
references.reference: Professor Longbottom has exceeded every expectation I had when I appointed him, and my expectations were already high. He has built the Herbology programme into one of the finest in Britain while simultaneously serving as an exemplary Head of House. His commitment to student welfare — particularly to students who carry the weight of the war years — reflects the very best of Gryffindor values. I will not pretend he was my most promising student when in his first year. He has earned the right to find that funny.

highlights: Led annual Forbidden Forest botanical surveys, discovering and formally documenting two previously uncatalogued magical plant species in the castle grounds

Launched the Hogwarts Rare Wizarding Flora Preservation Programme, a collaboration with international magical institutions, cataloguing and preserving seeds and cuttings of endangered magical plant species

Expanded the Hogwarts greenhouse complex to seven structures, adding specialist facilities for venomous, carnivorous, and magically-active plant species, providing controlled environments for observation and study
Supervised 34 N.E.W.T.-level independent research projects, with twelve students pursuing careers in Herbological research or magical plant protection
Developed a post-war trauma-sensitive teaching approach, particularly for students who experienced Hogwarts under Death Eater administration, applicable to diverse field environments
Served as Head of Gryffindor House since 2003, overseeing pastoral care and scholarship guidance, demonstrating strong mentoring capabilities
work.name: Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
work.summary: Responsible for delivering advanced Herbology instruction and managing a world-leading greenhouse complex. Pioneered field research in magical botany, leading to significant discoveries and contributions to the conservation of endangered species. Expert in the identification, cultivation, and safe handling of a wide array of magical plants, including those with hazardous properties. Contributes to scientific documentation and mentors aspiring magical researchers.

highlights: Participated in the capture of six Death Eaters during active field operations in 1998–1999, demonstrating tactical effectiveness and composure in hazardous environments
Commended by Head Auror Harry Potter for exceptional composure and tactical effectiveness during field operations
Completed the full Auror training programme in twelve months despite no formal post-Hogwarts qualification, showcasing rapid adaptation and learning in field operative skills
Contributed firsthand field notes on Death Eater tactics and safe houses that informed twelve successful warrant operations

Remained on reserve call-up with the Auror Office following transition to teaching; participated in two subsequent special operations in 2002 and 2005, indicating ongoing readiness for field deployment
work.name: Ministry of Magic — Auror Office
work.summary: Served as a trained Auror in post-war Ministry field operations, focusing on the identification and apprehension of dangerous individuals. Gained extensive experience in remote field deployment, tactical operations, and maintaining composure under extreme pressure. Developed robust observational and reporting skills essential for critical intelligence gathering.

highlights: Reformed and led Dumbledore's Army in September 1997 during Death Eater occupation, demonstrating exceptional leadership and resilience under extreme duress
Established and maintained a residential refuge in the Room of Requirement for at-risk students, ensuring sustainable housing, food, and communication infrastructure for up to twenty individuals
Coordinated supply lines into Hogwarts throughout the 1997–98 academic year using external contacts, showcasing logistical planning and resourcefulness
Personally led DA fighters to facilitate the entry of Harry Potter and allies into the castle, initiating the Battle of Hogwarts
Commanded a section of Hogwarts's defensive perimeter during the Battle, directing student fighters and coordinating with staff and Order members
Destroyed Nagini (Voldemort's final Horcrux) with the Sword of Gryffindor, an act of unparalleled bravery that directly enabled the defeat of Lord Voldemort
work.name: Dumbledore's Army — Hogwarts Resistance
work.summary: Led student resistance operations during the Death Eater occupation of Hogwarts, demonstrating extraordinary leadership, strategic planning, and crisis management skills under hostile conditions. Responsible for protecting vulnerable students, maintaining morale, and coordinating the defence of the castle during the Second Wizarding War. Proven ability to operate independently and decisively in high-risk, unsupervised environments.
